goal.textColor: Color of the title and numbers.
goal.fullColor: The bar's color once the target is reached.
goal.bg: **Color**: a box behind the goal. **Transparent**: a box without fill. **Off**: no box.
goal.bgOpacity: How solid the box is. 0% is see-through.
goal.radius: How round the corners of the box and the bar are.
goal.scale: Makes the whole goal bigger or smaller. Above 100%, make the OBS source bigger too.
goal.fontSize: Size of the title and numbers.
goal.font: The typeface of the goal's text.
goal.titlePos: The title above or below the bar, inside it, or hidden.
goal.showPercent: Shows how far along it is, for example 64%.
goal.showNumbers: Shows the count and the target, for example 32 / 50.
goal.celebrate: Confetti and a glow, once, when the target is reached.
goal.kickSync: Goals you set on your Kick channel (Kick's creator dashboard: followers, subscriptions, KICKs) show Kick's own count and target, here and on stream: read every minute, and at once when Kick sends a change. A goal with nothing set on Kick stays as you set it here. If Kick can't be reached, the last numbers stay.

It needs your Twitch account connected on **Connections**. A goal with nothing set on Twitch stays as you set it here.

chat.kickChannel: Your channel name, as in `kick.com/name`. Brings the chat and real Kick alerts. No login.

chat.badgeSize: How big badges are next to the name. 100% is as tall as the name.
chat.badgeBg: A small dark square behind Kick's and Twitch's own badges (OG, mod, VIP, verified, founder, broadcaster, staff, sub gifter), which are made for dark chats. **Auto**: only where the message background is light. **Always**: on every message. **Off**: never. Sub badges never get one.
chat.ogHat: Kick viewers with the OG badge get a black hat with MP on it.
chat.hatStyle: The hat: a cap, a beanie or a fedora.
chat.hatPos: **First letter** / **Last letter**: on the name. **Badge**: a small hat with the badges, instead of the OG badge. **Profile picture**: on the picture (with profile pictures off: on the first letter).
chat.showTime: The time each message was sent.
chat.showColon: A colon between the name and the message.
chat.emotesKick: Kick emotes as pictures. Off: their names show as text.
chat.emotesTwitch: Twitch emotes as pictures. Off: their names show as text.
chat.emotes7tv: 7TV emotes (the channel's and the global ones) as pictures.
chat.emotesAnimated: Animated emotes move. Off: they stand still.
chat.bigEmotes: A message with only emotes shows them bigger.
chat.nameColorMode: **Platform color**: each name's own color from Kick or Twitch. **Style colors**: the style's. **One color**: the same for everyone.
chat.readableNames: A platform color that is hard to read on the box (light on light, dark on dark) gets just enough lighter or darker to read well. It stays the same color.
chat.namePos: The name on the same line as the message, or above it.
chat.textShadow: A soft shadow that keeps text readable on busy backgrounds.
chat.textDir: **Auto** puts Persian and Arabic messages right to left, everything else left to right.
chat.bg: **Color**: a box behind the chat. **Transparent**: a box without fill. **Off**: no box.
chat.bgOpacity: How solid the box is. 0% is see-through.
chat.bubbles: Each message in its own bubble instead of one big box.
chat.padding: Space inside the box, around the messages.
chat.width: Width of the chat. Make the OBS source at least this wide.
chat.height: Height of the chat. Make the OBS source at least this tall.
chat.layout: **Vertical**: a list of messages. **Horizontal**: one bar where messages scroll by.
chat.tickerDir: Which way messages move along the bar.
chat.tickerSpeed: How fast the bar moves, in pixels per second.
chat.tickerLoop: When chat is quiet, the bar keeps showing the last messages again.
chat.tickerPos: Puts the bar at the top or the bottom of a taller OBS source.
chat.maxMessages: How many messages stay on screen; older ones leave.
chat.hideAfter: Each message leaves after this many seconds. 0 = never.
chat.enterAnim: How a new message comes in.
chat.animSpeed: Faster or slower animations. ×2 is twice as fast.
chat.fade: Old messages fade out softly at the edge instead of being cut off.
chat.fadeZone: How big that soft edge is.
chat.typewriter: The newest message is typed out letter by letter.
chat.typeSound: A soft typing sound while it types.
chat.hideCommands: Hides messages that start with `!`, like `!discord`.
chat.hideBots: Hides messages from the names in **Bots**.
chat.bots: Bot names to hide, separated by commas.
chat.hiddenUsers: Viewers whose messages never show, separated by commas.
chat.blockedWords: A message with any of these words is hidden. Separate them with commas.
chat.hideLinks: Hides messages that contain a link.
chat.source: Both chats, only Kick, or only Twitch.
chat.fxSubGlow: Sub lines glow gold, with a SUBSCRIBER tag. While special sub lines are on (above), a sub gets that line instead: this is for the other sub lines, like the viewers a gift went to.
chat.fxFirst: A viewer's very first message in your chat gets a sparkly tag.
chat.fxRainbowVip: VIPs' names shine in rainbow colors.
chat.rainbowUsers: More names that get the rainbow, separated by commas.
chat.fxMention: Messages that mention your channel name stand out.
chat.fxCombo: When people send the same emote again and again, it shows once with a counter (x12).
chat.avatars: Profile pictures next to names. Kick: real pictures, or Kick's own default picture for viewers without one. Twitch: real pictures too (no key needed), or the first letter of the name when one can't be found.
chat.blur: Blurs what's behind a see-through box, like frosted glass.
chat.showTiming: For finding chat delays. Each new message gets a small label like `+1.2s`: how long after Kick or Twitch made it, it showed here. The window where Jarchi runs prints one line per message with each step: **received** (Jarchi got it), **sent** (to the chat), **shown** (the chat drew it). Turn it off when you're done.
chat.enabled: Off: the chat is hidden on stream. Kick and Twitch stay connected, so alerts still come.
chat.eventKicks: A special line when someone sends Kicks, with Kick's gift picture, its name and what it's worth: **LifeWing sent HELL YEAH ×1 · 1 Kicks**, then their message.
chat.eventKicksMin: Gifts worth fewer Kicks than this get no line. 0 = every gift.
chat.eventSubs: Subs and resubs as a special line: **Ali subscribed for 6 months!**, then their message. Off: the usual sub line.
chat.eventGifts: Gifted subs as a special line: **Rich gifted 5 subs!** Off: the usual line.
chat.eventGiftsMin: Gifts of fewer subs than this keep the usual line. 0 = every gift.
chat.eventBits: A cheer as a special line, with Twitch's gem for the amount: **Sara cheered 500 bits!**, then the message. Off: the usual message.
chat.eventBitsMin: Cheers of fewer bits than this stay a usual message. 0 = every cheer.
chat.eventRaids: A special line when a channel raids you (on Kick: hosts you), with how many viewers came.
chat.eventLook: **Card**: a tinted card with a bar in Kick's green or Twitch's purple. **Glow**: a glowing ring. **Simple line**: just the words. Each works inside every chat style.
chat.eventLonger: Special lines stay on screen twice as long: twice the **Hide each message after** time, and until twice **Max messages on screen** newer ones came. In a bar they go by twice.

connections.clientId: The Twitch app Jarchi logs in with. Jarchi's own is filled in and works for everyone. To use your own instead, make one at dev.twitch.tv/console (**Register Your Application**, Client Type **Public**) and paste its **Client ID** here. Empty the field to go back to Jarchi's.

settings.showBadge: A small Kick or Twitch badge on alerts. It only shows when both accounts are connected.
settings.testAs: Which platform test alerts come from. `{platform}` in the alert text shows its name.
settings.alertGap: Seconds of quiet between two alerts.
settings.proxyMode: How Jarchi reaches Kick, Twitch and 7TV: directly, through the Windows proxy your VPN sets, or through a proxy you type in.
settings.proxyType: Your VPN or proxy app tells you which. v2rayN: SOCKS5 on `10808`, HTTP on `10809`.
settings.proxyHost: The proxy's address. For a VPN app on this PC: `127.0.0.1`.
settings.obsUrl: The alerts link for OBS. Add it as a Browser Source, 1920 × 1080.

start.title: Getting started
start.intro: Jarchi runs on your own PC and shows alerts, a chat box and goals in OBS. No account and no login: your Kick and Twitch channel names are enough for real alerts.
steps: Keep Jarchi running
Start Jarchi and leave its window open while you stream. This panel is at `{panelUrl}`.
Type your channel names
Open **Chat** in the menu and type your Kick and/or Twitch channel. Each name also brings that platform's real alerts.
Pick a theme
Open **Alerts** and click **Theme** at the top. Every alert uses it, unless you give an alert its own.
Add Jarchi to OBS
Add the alerts to OBS as a Browser Source. The next topic shows how.
Test it
In **Alerts**, pick an alert in the list and press **Test in OBS**. It plays in OBS and shows up in the alert queue.
start.tip: Start Jarchi before OBS. If OBS was open first, right-click the Jarchi source in OBS and choose **Refresh**.

obs.title: Add Jarchi to OBS
obs.intro: Every part of Jarchi is a web page that OBS shows as a Browser Source. The alerts, the chat and each goal have their own link.
steps: Copy the link
On the **Alerts** page, click **Copy OBS link**. The alerts link is `{alertsUrl}`.
Add a Browser Source
In OBS: **Sources → + → Browser**. Give it a name, for example "Jarchi Alerts".
Paste it and set the size
Paste the link into **URL**. Width **1920**, height **1080**.
Turn on the sound
Tick **Control audio via OBS**, so alert sounds go through the OBS mixer to your stream. Then click **OK**.
Chat and goals
The same steps, with their own link and size. Chat: `{chatUrl}`, 420 × 600. Goals: `{goalSubsUrl}` and `{goalKicksUrl}`, 800 × 200 (Circle style: 400 × 400).
obs.tip: Jarchi must be running when OBS loads the source. If you started OBS first, right-click the source and choose **Refresh**. After that it reconnects by itself whenever Jarchi restarts.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.intro: Seven alerts: follow, sub, resub, gifted subs, Kicks, bits and raid. Each has its own picture, sound and text.
steps: Pick an alert
Click it in the **Alerts** list. The switch next to it turns it on or off; the Kick and Twitch logos show where it comes from.
Preview it

The preview plays the alert exactly as OBS will, and again after every change. **Replay** plays it once more, **Dark**, **Light** and **Checkered** change only the preview's background, and **Test in OBS** sends it to OBS.
Media, Sound, Text, Style

The four tabs under the preview. **Media**: your own image, GIF or video (or the theme's), how long it stays, the minimum amount. **Sound**: the theme's, your own or none, the volume, a video's sound. **Text**: the words (`{user}` `{amount}` `{months}` `{platform}` become the real values), position, size and color. **Style**: a theme for this alert only, and the frame.
Different media by amount
In **Media**, Kicks, gifted subs and bits can play their own picture and sound for bigger amounts. Turn it on and upload per amount.
No Save button
Every change saves by itself, text a moment after you stop typing. A small **Saved** at the bottom of the page says it's done.
alerts.tip: Real Kick alerts (subs, resubs, gifted subs, Kicks and hosts) come from your Kick channel name in **Chat**, with no login. Real Twitch alerts (subs, resubs, gifted subs, raids and bits) come from your Twitch channel name the same way. Follows come once your Kick and Twitch accounts are connected on **Connections**. The **Test** buttons work for every alert.

goals.title: Goals
goals.intro: Six goals on two tabs. **Kick**: a Sub goal (subs, resubs and gifted subs), a Kicks goal and a Followers goal. **Twitch**: a Sub goal, a Bits goal and a Followers goal. Each one counts its own platform's events by itself, never the other's. With **Sync from Kick** or **Sync from Twitch** (at the top of each tab), a goal you also set on that channel shows that channel's own numbers.
steps: Open a goal
Open **Goals** and click a goal on the **Kick** or **Twitch** tab.
Title and target
Type the title viewers see and the number to reach.
Fix the count
In the list, click a goal's number and type another one, or press **Reset to 0** (twice) for a new goal. In the editor, **−** and **+** change it by one step. The count is kept when Jarchi restarts.
Pick a look
Choose a style, then change colors, box, font and size in **More options**. **Reset style** brings the style's own look back.
Add it to OBS
Click **Copy OBS link** and add it as a Browser Source, 800 × 200 (Circle style: 400 × 400).
goals.tip: When the target is reached, the bar turns the "full" color and celebrates once. The switch in the list only hides the goal on stream; it keeps counting.

chat.title: Chat widget
chat.intro: Kick and Twitch chat together in one box on your stream, with Kick, Twitch and 7TV emotes.
steps: Type your channels
On the **Chat** page, type your Kick and/or Twitch channel name. No login. Each one says **Connected** when it works.
Pick a style
18 vertical styles and 9 horizontal bars (**Vertical** / **Horizontal** above them). A style is a starting point: every option works with every style.
Try it
**Send test message** (the arrow next to it: **Send 10 messages**, **Show all effects**) fills the preview and OBS with sample messages. **Replay** plays the last ones again in the preview.
Fine-tune it
The tabs: **Text**, **Names & badges**, **Events** (special lines for Kicks, subs, gift subs, bits and raids), **Filters** and **Layout** (size, box and motion).
Add it to OBS
Click **Copy OBS link** and add it as a Browser Source, 420 × 600. Make it at least as big as the chat's width and height; the horizontal bars need width 1920.
chat.tip: The **Show the chat on stream** switch (under the preview) only hides the chat on stream. Real Kick and Twitch alerts keep coming either way.

queue.title: Alert queue
queue.intro: Alerts play one after another, never on top of each other. The **Alert queue** page shows what's playing and what's waiting.
steps: Now playing
The alert on screen, with a bar for the time it has left.
Pause, Skip, Clear
**Pause** lets the current alert finish and holds the rest. **Skip** ends the current one. **Clear queue** (click twice) removes everything waiting.
Waiting and Replay
× takes one waiting alert out. **Last played** keeps the last 10, each with **Replay**.
Gap between alerts
In **Settings**, choose how many seconds pass between two alerts.
queue.tip: If OBS is closed, alerts wait and play when it opens again; the page says so at the top. In the menu, the number next to **Alert queue** is how many alerts are waiting.

proxy.title: Proxy & VPN
proxy.intro: If Kick, Twitch or 7TV is filtered where you are, Jarchi can connect through your VPN or proxy. Chat pictures (emotes, badges, profile pictures) go through it too.
steps: Open the setting
**Settings → Connection (proxy)**.
Windows system proxy
The default. It uses the Windows proxy your VPN app sets. If none is set, Jarchi connects directly.
Manual
Pick HTTP or SOCKS5 and type your VPN app's local address and port, for example `127.0.0.1` and `10808` (SOCKS5 in v2rayN).
Test it
**Test connection** checks Kick, Twitch and 7TV and says in plain words what works.
proxy.tip: If your VPN runs in TUN mode (the whole PC goes through it), **Off** works too. Proxies with a username and password, and PAC scripts, aren't supported.

fix.title: If something doesn't work
fix.intro: Click a question to see what to check.

faq.q: The alert doesn't show in OBS
a: Is Jarchi running? Start it before OBS, or right-click the source in OBS and choose **Refresh**.
If the **Alert queue** page says the OBS overlay isn't open, OBS hasn't loaded the page. Check that the URL is exactly `{alertsUrl}`.
The source should be 1920 × 1080, visible, and in the scene you're live on.
Is the alert switched on in the list? Is the queue paused? Kicks below the **Minimum amount** (10 by default) don't play.
In the source's properties in OBS, tick **Control audio via OBS**, then check that the source isn't muted in the OBS mixer.
Check that the alert's **Sound** isn't **No sound**, and its **Volume** in the **Sound** tab.
The **Sound** box under the preview only mutes the preview here in the panel.
For a video with its own sound, choose **Video sound** in the **Sound** tab.

faq.q: Kick won't connect, or it's filtered
a: **channel not found**: type the name exactly as in your Kick link, `kick.com/name`.
**blocked** or **can't reach it**: Kick is filtered or blocked on your network. Turn on your VPN, set up **Settings → Connection (proxy)** and press **Test connection**.
Jarchi keeps retrying by itself; there's no need to restart it.
Does the channel say **Connected** under **Chat**? Is the chat switched on?
Send a test message. If it shows here but not in OBS, refresh the source in OBS and make it at least as big as the chat (420 × 600 is enough for the default style).
Check the filters: **Show from**, **Hidden users**, **Blocked words** and **Hide each message after**.

faq.q: Alerts are late or pile up
a: Alerts play one at a time, so a burst waits in line. Lower **Duration** or **Gap between alerts**, or use **Skip** and **Clear queue**.
Raise the Kicks alert's **Minimum amount** to keep small taps out of the line (goals still count them).
Kick sends some events a few seconds late, and an automatic resub waits about 10 seconds for its months. That's normal.
